title: Spicy Chili Oil Pork and Shrimp Wontons
summary: Juicy pork and shrimp wontons, boiled and drenched in a homemade Sichuan-style chili oil infused with shallot, star anise and black cardamom, finished with green onion.
notes: Video: 'Spicy Chili Garlic Wontons At Home' on the Joshua Weissman Recipes channel (UCUAg71CJEvFdOnujmep1Svw). Auto-generated captions; evidence is quoted as they read. Written recipe: https://www.joshuaweissman.com/recipes/the-best-spicy-chili-oil-wontons-recipe (serves 6, prep 30 min, cook 45 min; the page embeds this video). Every chili-oil and filling amount is stated in the video and matches the written recipe; grams for the chili flakes (40 g), mushroom seasoning (7 g) and MSG (3 g) come from the page. Optional items he adds on camera count (rule 11): the mushroom seasoning, the MSG in the filling and the raw garlic stirred into the oil. Judgment call: the chili oil is a storable batch (about 2 1/4 cups) and only part of it goes on the wontons. Spooned over the dish, it counts (house rule), but neither the video nor the page states the share used, so house rule 10 applies: a spooned-over spice oil counts at 25% of the batch (about 9 Tbsp, 1 1/2 Tbsp per serving). Every chili-oil line keeps the full batch amount in its text and shows the 25% in its quantity and note. The shallots, whole spices, 7 garlic cloves and cinnamon stick are strained out of the oil and not counted. Ranges: raw garlic in the oil 2-3 cloves (midpoint), ginger 2-3 tsp (midpoint; the page's 2-inch knob would be heavier), 30-40 wontons (midpoint 35 wrappers at USDA's 8 g). Green onion garnish: 1 bunch on the page, about 7 onions (our estimate). Not counted: the optional black vinegar on the side and the boiling water. Proxies: toasted rapeseed oil uses canola oil; Sichuan chili flakes use cayenne; black vinegar uses balsamic vinegar; Sichuan peppercorn, star anise and black cardamom (all excluded) use black pepper, anise seed and cardamom. A separate component file for the chili oil was not written.

steps.text: Chili oil: put the neutral oil and toasted rapeseed oil in a small pot with the shallots, Sichuan peppercorns, star anise, black cardamom, whole garlic and cinnamon stick, all submerged.
Over medium-low, hold the oil at about 250°F, stirring now and then, for 20-30 minutes, until the aromatics are very soft and deeply browned.
Strain out the aromatics, then heat the oil alone to 350°F (left in, they would burn).
In a large heat-proof bowl, whisk the chili flakes with the sesame seeds, mushroom seasoning, sugar, kosher salt, MSG and black vinegar.
Standing back, carefully pour the 350°F oil over the chili mixture (it foams hard) and whisk until all the chili is saturated.
Optionally, once the oil has cooled slightly, stir in 2-3 finely chopped raw garlic cloves. Cool to room temperature, then store covered in the fridge.
Filling: very finely chop the shrimp with a knife, slicing thinly one way and then across, until almost a paste.
Add the shrimp to the ground pork with the grated garlic and ginger, kosher salt, sugar, MSG, soy sauce and finely chopped green onion. Knead and fold like a dough until evenly mixed and tacky.
Spoon the filling into a piping bag (optional, but faster).
Cup a wonton wrapper in your hand, less-starchy side up. Pipe filling into it until full to the edges, pinch it off at the bag and press the top closed. Makes 30-40.
Boil the wontons in batches (or from frozen) for 2-3 minutes, until the filling is firm and the wrapper soft.
Lift them out with a spider, drain, and serve in bowls topped generously with chili oil and sliced green onion, with a little black vinegar on the side if you like.
